purpose: Source-attributed public reference corpus for cargo-vessel propulsion architecture research. Values are not transferable performance predictions.

sources.title: Wind-propelled ships for maritime decarbonization: Technologies, global deployment, and engineering challenges
sources.publisher: International Journal of Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering

scope.study_type: multi-source ship-level deployment inventory and technology review

observations.statement: Review inventory identified 96 ships equipped with wind propulsion systems by the end of 2025.
The review reported 90 of the 96 inventoried ships still in service at the end of 2025.

limitations: Multi-source inventory coverage depends on public reports and source availability.
The ship count is not a measure of fuel saved, operational availability, or economic return.
Device-level savings are route-, vessel-, weather-, control- and service-dependent.
Do not infer a universal percentage benefit from fleet adoption counts.
ineligible_use: Direct prediction of savings for a new vessel
Proof of economic viability for a specific ship
Measured device reliability without underlying service records

sources.title: Integrated Design and Dynamic Performance Optimisation of Hybrid Electric Propulsion Systems for Coastal Cargo Vessels Under Real-World Operational Profiles

scope.candidate: diesel generator sets, DC bus, propulsion motors and lithium-ion battery storage
scope.design_method: bi-level sizing optimization with dynamic-programming energy management and battery degradation-aware lifecycle cost

observations.statement: The article reports 16-21% fuel savings for its optimized hybrid configuration relative to its mechanical baseline.
The article reports 17-20% CO2 reduction relative to its mechanical baseline.
The article reports 8-14% lifecycle cost reduction relative to its mechanical baseline.
The optimized case reports 2.3 MW installed generator power compared with 6.0 MW in its mechanical baseline.
The optimized case reports a 1.6 MWh battery energy storage system.

limitations: This is a specific coastal cargo case, not a deep-sea container-ship result.
The article uses reconstructed AIS/logbook operating profiles and a model-based optimization; it is not an independent sea-trial measurement of the claimed savings.
The authors identify simplified resistance/propulsion modeling and incomplete representation of fouling, extreme weather and manoeuvring.
The lower-level offline dynamic-programming controller assumes perfect knowledge of future voyage power profiles.
Do not transfer percentages, installed power or battery size to another route/vessel.
eligible_use: Baseline for a coastal-vessel branch of the programme

sources.title: CFD-based approaches for low-carbon shipping: A systematic review

scope.study_type: systematic review of CFD applications in hull form, surface drag, propeller/wake, wind integration and operational approaches

observations.basis: review-reported upper range across heterogeneous studies

limitations: The review synthesizes heterogeneous geometries, regimes, methods and validation levels.
The ranges are not additive and must not be combined into a synthetic total saving.
These are not guaranteed improvements for a target cargo vessel.
Use as a literature landscape and candidate-mechanism map, not as a design input without source-case reproduction.
eligible_use: Range sanity checks when source studies are individually retrieved
ineligible_use: Independent validation of a new hull or surface treatment

sources.title: Design and Optimisation of Future-Oriented Ships

capability_description: aero- and hydrodynamics for overall ship system
load, power and movement profiles from transport task and historical weather
energy and propulsion system evaluation and optimization

limitations: Public capability description is not a reproducible benchmark result.
No quantitative prediction-accuracy, cost or fuel-saving metric is inferred from this page.
Detailed software access, model fidelity and validation corpora are not established by the public description alone.
ineligible_use: Assumption that unreported functionality is absent

sources.title: SHIPFLOW: CFD for ships

capability_description: automated design workflows and CAESES integration

limitations: Vendor capability page is not independent performance validation.
No benchmark result or quantitative accuracy figure is inferred from the public page.
Detailed capabilities must be assessed on an identical case and solver-validation basis.

sources.title: Ships and marine technology — Specifications for the assessment of speed and power performance by analysis of speed trial data

scope.purpose: Analysis of ship speed-power trial data for prescribed conditions, including environmental corrections within the standard's applicability.

limitations: The standard is a method reference, not a ship-performance data source.
Applicability and required corrections must be determined by qualified personnel for the vessel and trial.
This project must not invent or claim ISO conformity from a simplified calculation.

sources.title: Ships and marine technology — Measurement of changes in hull and propeller performance — Part 1: General principles

scope.purpose: General principles and performance indicators for measuring changes in hull and propeller performance over time.

limitations: The published scope focuses on conventional fixed-pitch propeller ships and compares the same ship to itself over time.
Do not treat it as a general inter-vessel architecture-ranking method.
Check current applicability and edition at the time of any formal trial.
eligible_use: In-service hull/propeller maintenance and retrofit measurement reference
ineligible_use: Direct comparison of unlike ship designs

sources.title: Ships and marine technology — Measurement of changes in hull and propeller performance — Part 2: Default method

scope.purpose: Default method and basic performance indicators for measuring hull and propeller performance changes over time on applicable vessel types.

limitations: The published scope is centered on commercial displacement ships with conventional fixed-pitch propellers.
It is primarily same-vessel before/after measurement, not a universal comparison standard across vessel types.
Normative procedures are not reproduced in this registry.
ineligible_use: Claim of compliance without qualified method execution

sources.title: Ship Energy Efficiency Solutions Portal

examples: kites, fixed sails, wings and Flettner rotors
trim, draft, speed and autopilot optimization

limitations: Savings and applicability vary by vessel type and operation.
Portal descriptions are not a matched evaluation of one candidate vessel.
Do not sum individual measure estimates without interaction and double-counting analysis.

sources.title: Nuclear Reactors for Merchant Shipping: A Total Cost of Ownership Assessment of a Low-Carbon Pathway

scope.metric: total cost of ownership normalized by transport work

observations.statement: The published summary states no nuclear option is cheaper than conventional ships without the IMO Net-Zero Framework, even under the lowest reactor-cost assumptions.
The published summary describes nuclear as potentially least cost from 2040 only if reactor costs fall substantially to levels not yet demonstrated.

limitations: The result is conditional on the modelled policy and reactor-cost assumptions.
Insurance, liability and regulatory frameworks remain major barriers.
This is not a wind-assist study and is not a direct comparator for the hybrid cargo case.
Use the admitted source-specific inputs and full study boundary for reproduction.
eligible_use: Economic policy sensitivity and fuel-system architecture reference

sources.title: Power Shift: Nuclear Power Pathways for Future Containership Fleets
sources.publisher: Lloyd's Register Advisory / LucidCatalyst (case for Seaspan)

scope.comparison_context: public case study compares a higher-speed nuclear-powered case with conventional vessel operations

observations.statement: The public summary reports up to 38% greater annual cargo capacity.
The public summary reports up to 5% additional container space from removing fuel tanks and systems.
Public summary uses five annual round voyages for the conventional comparison.
Public summary uses 6.3 annual round voyages for the nuclear-powered case.

limitations: Public summary is insufficient to reconstruct all route, demand, cost, utilization and operating assumptions.
These are modelled case-study outputs, not measured fleet outcomes.
The higher annual cargo figure includes speed and space effects and must not be attributed solely to propulsion energy efficiency.
Do not directly compare against the UCL TCO model without a transparent boundary bridge.
This is not a wind-assist study.
ineligible_use: Universal vessel speed or throughput claim
Direct economic comparison without source-specific reproduction
